subject: Zenith Consulting — architecture readout and test schedule
messages:
From: Sarah Liu <sarah.liu@zenithconsult.com>
To: sergio_alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Turner <alex.turner@zenithconsult.com>
Date: 2027-06-30T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Zenith/Redwood — architecture readout + next steps

Hi Sergio,

Thanks again for the intro last week. As discussed, we pulled together an initial reference architecture and a proposed test schedule so we can validate integration points between Zenith's connector framework and Redwood's private deployment model. Attached: zenith-reference-arch.pdf (diagram + sequence flows) and a working test plan (zenith-test-plan.xlsx).

Key asks from our side to keep the POC focused:
- Confirm supported auth flows (API key vs. OIDC) for private deployment.
- Quick compatibility check on Redwood's KV cache behavior when requests come from our streaming pipeline.
- Acceptance criteria for the latency SLO in the test plan (we proposed 95th percentile < 200ms for inference requests under 50 RPS).

Can we get a 30–45 minute architecture readout this week? Laura and Marissa from Redwood were suggested — copying them now.

Thanks,
Sarah Liu
Principal Architect, Zenith Consulting
Attachments: zenith-reference-arch.pdf (diagram, 2.1MB), zenith-test-plan.xlsx (sheets: scope, test-cases, metrics)
From: sergio_alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Liu <sarah.liu@zenithconsult.com>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-30T10:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Zenith/Redwood — architecture readout + next steps

Hi Sarah — welcome, and thanks for sending the materials. Attachments look clear. We can run a short readout and then step into the validation plan. Quick answers up-front:
- Redwood Private supports API key auth today for our on-prem and VPC variants; OIDC is on our roadmap and we have a supported workaround (short-lived signed assertions via our connector).
- KV cache semantics are per-model variant — caching is prefix-aware and we can expose cache hit/miss metrics to your telemetry.
- The latency SLO you propose (95 pctl < 200ms at 50 RPS) is reasonable for smaller models; we'll validate across the model family you list in the test plan.

Laura, Marissa — can one of you run the readout? Sarah suggested Thursday (7/1) afternoon PT. If that doesn't work, Friday morning PT is fine. After the readout we'd like to align on the test runner artifact (we can provide a lightweight harness) and the failure modes you care most about (timeouts, cold-starts, semantic regressions).

Sergio
Head of Partner Engineering, Redwood Inference
From: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Liu <sarah.liu@zenithconsult.com>, sergio_alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-30T11:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Zenith/Redwood — architecture readout + next steps

Hi Sarah — happy to run the readout. Proposed agenda (30–40 min):
1) 5m introductions & goals
2) 10m architecture walk-through (Zenith diagram)
3) 10m Redwood runtime touchpoints (auth, routing, caching, observability)
4) 10m test plan and acceptance criteria
5) 5m immediate next steps & owners

We have an internal checklist (redwood-integration-checklist.md) that maps tests to infra requirements — I'll attach and reference during the session. For scheduling: I'm available Thursday 7/1 from 1:00–3:00pm PT or Friday 7/2 9:30–11:00am PT. Pick a slot and I'll send a calendar invite with a short shared Drive link.

Also tagging Marissa for the telemetry requirements and Aditya for a quick note on the test harness (we can offer a dockerized load generator).

Laura Bennett
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachments: redwood-integration-checklist.md
From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@zenithconsult.com>
To: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, sergio_alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>, Sarah Liu <sarah.liu@zenithconsult.com>
Date: 2027-07-01T08:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Zenith/Redwood — architecture readout + next steps

Thanks — Friday 7/2 10:00am PT works for Zenith on our side. A couple of clarifications ahead of the readout so we can keep the session technical and action-focused:
- We'll demonstrate a basic streaming flow that keeps an open session to Redwood (websocket/HTTP2) and enumerates token-level latencies. Can you confirm Redwood supports streaming over HTTP2 in Private?
- For auth, we'll try API key today but would like to exercise the signed-assertion flow for our production sim; any docs we should read?
- We'll include tests for cold-start behavior; on your end what metrics should we push back to the Drive so we can correlate traces?

Attachments: updated-test-cases.csv (small additions)

On the calendar invite — please include the Drive link and a short note on the DNS / network requirements for the private deployment (we have a constrained corporate network).

—Alex
Engineering Lead, Zenith Consulting
From: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@zenithconsult.com>, Sarah Liu <sarah.liu@zenithconsult.com>
Cc: sergio_alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-07-02T16:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Zenith/Redwood — architecture readout + next steps

Great — invite sent for Friday 2027-07-02 10:00am PT (30 min). Drive link and the three attachments are on the event. Quick technical notes ahead of the call:
- Streaming: Redwood Private supports server-sent events and HTTP/2 streaming for inference responses on the private control plane. We'll include a short demo snippet in the readout repo.
- Signed assertions: I'll drop a short how-to in the Drive (workaround) and the spec is at the Doc link in the materials.
- Telemetry: please push the following to correlate with our traces: request_id, model_version, kv_cache_hit, latency_ms, and node_id. We'll map those to our dashboards.
- DNS/network: inbound to your test harness should allow outbound TLS to the private control plane endpoint and UDP DNS resolution; port list is in the Drive doc.

Next steps after the readout: 1) Zenith runs the initial suite against a staging Private instance (we'll provision), 2) Redwood verifies results and lists any blockers, 3) 1-week iterative pass to close gaps.

Thanks all — looking forward to the session.

Laura Bennett
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
Attachments on invite: zenith-reference-arch.pdf, zenith-test-plan.xlsx, redwood-integration-checklist.md
